messages:
maya: Heads up — CI synthetic run flagged a perf regression on the canary after merge 0f3a2b. Canary autopause kicked in.
rick: Link to job? saw a flurry of alerts but need the trace. :eyes:
rick: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/31245 — p95 latency up ~35% in the canary window
maya: quick snippet from the synthetic run log:
```
model: rwd-13b-v2
sequence: mix(32, 512)
baseline p95: 120ms -> canary p95: 162ms (+35%)
kv_hit_rate: 0.81 -> 0.62
batch_size_avg: 6.2 -> 5.1
kernel_hint: enabled (autoselect-v2)
```
deploy-bot: Canary autopause executed: rollout paused at 2142345678 due to p95 SLO breach :warning:
evan: I started a local bisect — seems to correlate with PR #432 which introduced kernel-autoselect heuristic changes and a small prefetch tweak
josh: Confirming telemetry: on one canary host kv miss rate jumped from ~2% to ~17% after the canary image. That explains extra backend fetches and tail latency.
tina: Oof. Kernel autoselect changed prefetch window; possible it moves KV layout and evicts more prefixes. Can someone paste the eviction profile?
evan: here's an excerpt from perf profiler (aligned to canary window):
```
KV eviction spikes aligned with kernel selection transition
prefetch_work_ms increased by ~45% in the hot path
cpu util stable, but io waits up
``` 
rick: Two paths: revert PR #432 OR push a hotfix to disable the new prefetch option in the runtime config. Which is faster?
maya: Rollback first for safety. We don't want canary sitting paused for too long but it's blocking staged rollout. I can open a revert PR now.
josh: Agree on revert as emergency. Also we should expand canary guardrails: right now we only check p95/p99 token latency and error rate. Add KV hit-rate delta and a synthetic with long-prefix mixing.
tina: Proposed guardrail additions:
- fail canary if p95 increases > 15% vs baseline OR p99 > 20% OR kv_hit_rate drops > 5pp
- run CI synthetic with 30% long-context sequences to exercise KV cache
- add kernel-hint telemetry to canary health event stream
maya: Sounds good. @evan can you file the follow-up after revert? Include perf profile and a checklist for the canary SLO additions.
evan: On it. Will include a small patch to the CI job to include kv_hit_rate metric and a quick synthetic scenario.
rick: For immediate action: maya, submit revert PR. deploy-bot, once revert is merged trigger canary redeploy and re-run synthetic.
deploy-bot: Acknowledge. Will watch for the revert merge and kick the canary pipeline.
josh: Also adding one mitigator: if kernel-autoselect is desired, let's gate it behind a config flag per-model and default to previous hint for now.
tina: I'll draft the model-config flag RFC and link it in the follow-up.
maya: Revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/439 — tagging @oncall and runtime owners. Reverting kernel-autoselect change.
rick: Great. After revert we should run a short A/B with the previous heuristics vs the new one on a small traffic slice (non-critical) to collect more data before reintroducing.
maya: Agreed. I'll also add an item to the release checklist to include kv_hit_rate delta and prefetch_work_ms in the release notes perf checks.
evan: TL;DR: emergency revert, then follow-up to harden canary SLOs to include KV metrics and synthetic long contexts. I'll produce a short postmortem once we have numbers. :white_check_mark:
maya: Thanks all — keeping the thread here for visibility. If you have quick reproductions drop them here.
